Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the p assing away of Pandit Kishan 
Maharaj, an eminent tabla Maestro, on 4th May, 2008 at the age of 84 years.  
Born in Varanasi in September 1923, Pandit Kishan M aharaj began playing tabla 
when he was still a child. Initially, he learned the art from his father, Pandit Hari Maharaj, 
and, thereafter, he came under the tutelage of his uncle, Pandit Kanthe Maharaj, one of the 
great mastery of his time, from whom he started tak ing his lessons further. Pandit Kishan 
Maharaj had the ability to play cross-rhythms, part icularly, in tihai patterns which made 
him one of the most popular and cherished tabla players of his time. Pandit Kishan Maharaj 
had the distinction of playing any kind of accompan iment, be it with the Sitar, Sarod, 
Dhrupad, Dhamar or dance. His enthralling solo conc erts and jugalbandis with 
accomplished artistes would be long remembered.  
In the passing away of Pandit Kishan Maharaj, the m usic world has lost one of the 
greatest tabla Macstros of our time.

Special tourism status to Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand  
*561. SHRIAMIRALAM KHAN: Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:  
(a)  the States which have been accorded special tourism status; 
(b)  the funds allocated by Government to each of such S tates during the last three

(c)  whether there is any proposal to accord special tou rism status to Uttar Prade 
Uttarakhand;   
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  by when the decision is likely to be taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRIMATIAMBIKA SONI): (a) Ministry of Tourism, 
Government of India does not have any scheme for according special tourism status to States.  
(b) to (e) Do not arise. However, the Ministry of Tourism extends financial assistance to 
State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for tourism related projects, identified

Supply of gas  through pipelines in the country  
*562. SHRI K.AMALAKHTAR: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL 
GAS be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether there is any proposal to supply cooking gas to consumers through pipelines in 
the country, particularly in Jyotiba Phule Nagar and Moradabad in Uttar Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c)  the details of the funds sanctioned/spent so far an d the time schedule fixed for the 
completion of the scheme; 
(d)  the expected number of consumers to be benefited under this scheme; 
(e)  whether gas cylinders are likely to be taken from t he consumers covered under the 
scheme; and 
(0 if so, the details thereof?  
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
(a) to (d) Piped Natural Gas (PNG) is being supplied to domestic customers in Delhi, Noida, 
Mumbai and its suburbs, Agartala in Tripura and in various cities in Gujarat and Assam. As 
on 1 January, 2008, it is reported that PNG is being supplied to 802217 domestic consumers. 
The supply to these cities has been possible because of proximity to sources of gas and trunk 
gas pipelines. However, City Gas Distribution project has not been implemented in Jyotiba 
Phule Nagar and Moradabad, U.P.  
Government does not sanction/earmark funds for this  purpose. However, in order to 
promote investment from public as well as private sector for laying trunk natural gas pipelines 
and city/local natural gas distribution networks throughout the country, the Government of 
India has enacted 'The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006' and notified 
the 'Policy for Development of Natural Gas Pipeline s and City or Local Natural Gas 
Distribution Networks'.  
Providing of PNG facilities depends upon availabili ty of gas, setting up of necessary 
infrastructure and economic viability.  
(e) and (f) The Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies have been advised by Government 
to take measures to block connections of domestic LPG customers who are covered by PNG.

Investment in R & D activities 
*565.   SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: 
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:  
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:  
(a)  what is the investment both in amount as well as in  percentage in the Research and 
Development (R&D) activities of various Public Sect or Undertakings and institutes under 
the Ministry; 
(b)  whether it is a fact that investment in R & D is fa r below the level required for a 
country aspiring to emerge as economic super power;

(c)  what are the general norms for investment in R & D in various fields under their 
control; and 
(d)  how this percentage of investment is comparable wit h similar undertakings and 
institutes of the developed countries? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
(a) to (d) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas en courages initiation of Research & 
Development Projects by the Oil PSUs as also by oth er technical organizations like 
Centre for High Technology, Directorate of Hydrocar bons and Petroleum Conservation 
and Research Association.  
All these organizations have their own R&D wings wh ich are Undertaking research

There are no prescriptive norms for investment in R &D by Oil Sector Companies. 
Projects for R&D activities are taken up as per per ceived needs for development of new 
products/technologies and resolution of technical i ssues encountered by the Companies. 
Over the year, expenditure on R&D activities is on the increase and the Oil PSUs/other 
technical organizations under this Ministry are being provided all kinds of encouragement 
for taking up more & more R&D activities.

state:

THE MINISTER- OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVI ATION (SHRI

*-567. SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  whether instructions have been issued by the Reserv e Bank of India (RBI) for the 
Loan Waiver Scheme announced in the annual budget;

(d)  if so, the details thereof; 
(e)  whether Government has taken any decision for inclusion of farmers in the scheme 
who have taken loan from private moneylenders; and 
(f)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (0 The Debt 
Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme for farmers, announce d in the Union Budget 2008-09, 
stipulates waiver of all loans disbursed by State C ooperative Banks, Regional Rural 
Banks and Cooperative Credit Societies before 31.03 .2003, that were overdue on 
31.12.2007 and which remained unpaid until 29.02.20 08 for small farmers (land holding

of other farmers (land holding more than 2 hectares ), there is a One Time Settlement 
(OTS) Scheme for all loans that were overdue on 31. 12.2007 and which remained unpaid 
until 29.02.2008. The OTS provides a rebate of 25% against payment of the balance 
amount of 75%.  
The guidelines, which are in the process of being d rafted, will be issued by Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) and National Bank for Agricultu re and Rural Development 
(NABARD) to enable the implementation of the Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme by 
June 30,2008.

Regulation of micro financial agencies  
*571. SHRI M. V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government is in the proc ess of making a law called Micro 
Finance Sector Development and Regulation Bill to r egulate micro financial agencies in 
the country; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) and (b) The 
Government has introduced "The Micro Financial Sect or (Development and Regulation) 
Bill, 2007" in Lok Sabha on 20.03.2007 to provide a  formal statutory framework for the 
promotion, development and regulation of the micro finance sector. The Bill has been 
referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance. The salient features of this 
Bill are as follows:—  
(a)  entrust the function of development and regulation of the micro financial sector 
to the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (National Bank); 
(b)  define the various entitites engaged in the activit y of micro finance such as Co-
operative Societies, Mutual Benefit Societies or Mu tually Aided Societies 
registered under any State enactments or Multi Stat e Co-operative Societies 
registered under the Multi State Co-operative Socie ties Act, 2002, societies 
registered under the Societies Registration Act, 18 60 or any other State 
enactments governing such societies and a Trust cre ated under the Indian Trust 
Act, 1882 or public trust registered under any Stat e enactments, that will be 
governed by the regulatory framework proposed to be  set up; 
(c)  define various categories of beneficiaries of micro  financial services as eligible 
clients including Self Help Groups (SHGs) or joint liability groups of such 
eligible clients; 
(d)  provide for extending micro financial services to e ligible clients by way of 
financial assistance subject to ceilings to be pres cribed and such other financial 
services as may be specified by the National Bank; 
(e)  provide for acceptance of thrift i.e. savings of eligible clients other than in the 
form of current account or demand deposit account b y Micro Finance 
Organisations registered by the National Bank, subj ect to such terms and 
conditions as may be prescribed; 
(f)  provide for constitution of Micro Finance Developme nt Council to advise the 
National Bank on formulation of policies, schemes and other measures required 
in the interest of orderly growth and development of the micro finance sector; 
f 
(g) provide for registration of Micro Finance Organ isations to be permitted to  
collect thrift from individual members of SHGs or through a group mechanism;  
(h) provide for creation of a reserve fund and maintenance of accounts and periodical 
returns to be submitted by Micro Finance Organisations;

report released by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), many countries 
have resorted to restricting food exports and reduc ing restrictions on imports through 
tariff cuts to check price rise. According to the R eport, such price contro's and change in

*579. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES 
be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that a recent study by the Cen tral Ground Water Board 
(CGWB) had indicated that the ground water in over 200 districts of the country has a high 
level of flouride and aisenic, posing a big public-health hazard;

the worst placed with all its 32 districts at risk, while Orissa and Gujarat have 18 districts in

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (PROF. SA1F-UD-DIN SOZ): (a) to 
(c) The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) periodically monitors ground water quality 
at regional level. The analysis of samples has indicated high concentration of Fluoride and 
Arsenic in isolated pockets of 221 districts and 30 districts respectively, in various States.

litre and 0.01 milligram per litre respectively.

(i) Exploration is conducted by CGWB to find out gr ound water sources free from 
Arsenic/Fluoride contaminants.  
(ii) Technical guidance is provided to the State ag encies in tackling the problem of 
water quality and to take initiatives for capacity building of personnel of State Drinking 
Water Supply agencies.  
(iii) Financial and technical assistance is provide d to States under Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, namely Accelerated Rural Water Su pply Programme (ARWSP) for 
provision of safe drinking water to the rural population as per the stipulated norms.

Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) and Urban Infrastruc ture Development Scheme for

Strengthening the micro-finance sector  
4183. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Planning Commission in a report on stre ngthening the micro-finance 
sector has pointed out that there is an urgent need for the Centre to come out with a national 
policy on micro-finance with a view to financially empower the Below Poverty Line (BPL) 
families, reduce overall poverty in the country and evolve a coordinated strategy for a faster 
and smoother growth of the sector; 
(b)  if so, whether Government has considered the panel's recommendation; and 
(c)  if so, by when a final decision is likely to be taken on the matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) The Report of the Steering Committee on Microfinance and 
Poverty Alleviation (May 2007), constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri Anwarul Hoda, 
Member, Planning Commission, recommended the need for a concerted effort on the part of 
the various agencies and the service providers invo lved in the sector of microfinance to 
come together to evolve a coordinated strategy for a faster and smoother growth of the 
sector.  
The Government has already taken a number of steps for financial empowerment of 
Below Poverty Line farmers and other poor people. The constitution of the Financial Inclusion 
Fund (FIF) for meeting the cost of promotional and developmental interventions and the 
Financial Inclusion Technology Fund (FITF) for meet ing the cost of technology adoption, 
with an overall corpus of Rs. 500 crore each, are s teps in that direction.  
Further, the Government, in recent years, have also  initiated several measures in 
consultation with RBI and NABARD for financial empo werment of poor people. Banks 
have been instructed to achieve financial outreach through opening of "No Frills" accounts 
with limited overdraft facilities, to extend financ ial outreach by utilizing services of Civil 
Society Organisation like Farmers Clubs, NGOs, Post  Offices on the lines of Business 
Facilitator/Business Correspondent Model and to finance oral lessees and landless agricultural 
labourers through the Self Help Group and Joint Liability Group approach, etc.  
Besides, pursuant to the announcement in the Union Budget 2008-09, Government has 
advised Indian Banks' Association to suitably advis e the commercial banks to add at least 
250 rural household accounts every year at each of their rural and semi-urban branches.  
Selling of small under-performing public sector ban ks  
4184. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether a high level committee set up by Government has mooted a proposal to sell 
the small and under-performing public sector banks in the country; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether Government after reconsideration proposes t o merge the small and under-
performing public sector banks with profit earning banks rather than selling them; and 
(d)  if so, the reaction of Government in this regard? 

Written Answers to  [6 MAY 2008]  Unstarred Questions   41  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL): (a) and (b) With a view to outline a  comprehensive agenda for the 
evolution of the financial sector indicating especially the priorities and sequencing decision 
which the Government may keep in mind, Planning Com mission had set up a High Level 
Committee on Financial Sector Reforms headed by Shri Raghuram G. Rajan. On a proposal 
to sell small under-performing public sector banks, possibly to another bank or to a strategic 
investor, to gain experience with the process and gauge outcomes, the Committee has, in its 
draft report, opined as under:—  
"For the largest PSBs, the options are more limited . The selling of large PSBs to large 
private sector banks would raise issues of concentration. The selling of banks to industrial 
houses has been problematic across the world from t he perspective of financial stability 
because of the propensity of the houses to milk banks for "self-loans". Without a substantial 
improvement in the ability of the Indian system to curb related-party transactions, and to 
close down failing banks, this could be a recipe for financial disaster. While large international 
banks could swallow our largest banks, it is unlikely that this would be politically acceptable, 
at least in the foreseeable future. That leaves a sale through a public offering. But such a sale 
would require confidence in the corporate governanc e of these enterprises so that a high 
price can be realized. This Committee therefore bel ieves that the second aspect of the 
pragmatic approach, especially for large and better performing public sector banks, should 
be to focus on reforming the governance structure, while perhaps also acquiring strategic 
partners, with the eventual disposition determined based on experience with privatization, 
the public mood, and the political environment".  
The draft report is available at Planning Commissio n website 
www.planningcommission . nic. in.  
(c) and (d) There is no proposal to sell Government's stake in any public sector bank. As 
regards consolidation, Government is of the view that any such proposal by way of merger 
etc., of one public sector bank with another public  sector bank, should emanate from the 
concerned banks with Government playing a supportive role.

(a)  whether the Public Sector Undertaking (PSUs) like ONGC, IOC, NTPC, SAIL, etc.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL) : (a) Public Sector Companies are exp ected to pay dividend to the 
Government on the equity held by the Government as any other company would pay dividend 
to its shareholders. The interim dividend receipts for the year 2007-08 for public sector 
undertakings were estimated at Rs. 10,861 crore as per RE 2007-08. While ONGC, NTPC 
and SAIL have declared interim dividends of Rs. 3849.97 crore, Rs. 1992.50 crore and Rs.

(b) Dividend received by the Government from public sector undertakings forms part of 
Non-tax revenue receipts of the Government and thus contributes towards reducing the fiscal 
deficit. In the absence of interim dividend receipts, augmentation of tax revenues, other non-
tax revenues and non-debt capital receipts would be  required to achieve the targeted fiscal 
deficit as mandated under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 for

transactions. However, the new private sector banks such as ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Kotak 
Mahindra Bank, AXIS Bank, Yes Bank are actively dea ling in derivative products, which 
include Cross Currency Swaps, Currency Options. Cor porates often enter into derivative 
transactions with banks to hedge against adverse cu rrecy movements having bearing on 
their earnings. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that certain cases of alleged losses 
by the companies on account of dervicatives sold by  the banks have come to its notice. 
However, the existing Management Information System  of RBI does not generate the 
information about the loss caused to the companies or involvement of banks in legal suits on 
account of derivative transactions. 
To provide a framework for undertaking derivative t ransactions from a regulatory 
perpective, RBI has issued comprehensive guidelines on derivatives vide its circular dated 
20th April, 2007. the guidelines emphasise the need for a proper risk management framework 
and appropriate corporate governance practices. To protect the market-maker against the 
credit, reputation and litigation risks that may arise from a users' inadequate understanding 
of the nature and risks of the derivative transactions, the guidelines also provide that market-
makers should adopt a board approved 'Customer Appr opriateness and Suitability Policy' 
for derivative business. As a regulator of foreign exchange market, RBI also issues policy 
guidelines to Authorisied Dealers to facilitate residents/corporates in hedging their foreign 
currecy exposure by use of derivatives such as Forwards, Swaps and Options.  
(c) RBI takes up the irregularities/deficiencies ob served by its Inspecting Officers in

Statement  
Highlight of the comments of C&AG on performace audit report of ONGC relating to  
deep water exploration  
• The Company provided for less number of wells in th e 10th Five Year Plan (FYP) 
than what it committed to the Government of India/D irectorate General of 
Hydrocarbons. 
• The Company drilled six of the 16 wells committed i n the original grant period of 
four years in nine nomination blocks. Repeated exte nsion of time was allowed by 
paying PEL. 
• Scrutiny of 10 contracts awarded for seismic survey s revealed that due to lack of 
foresight in chartering and mobilizing the vessels for seismic survey, the Company 
lost a significant portion of the field seasons leading to delays in acquisition, processing 
and interpretation (API) of seismic data. 
• Delay in finalization of rig hiring contracts resulted in the Company not being able 
to have required number of rigs. Consequently, it d id not meet the commitment of 
drilling deep water wells leading to postponement o f drilling of eight wells during 
10th FYP. 
• The Company failed to monitor the actual cost of dr illing activities against their 
estimates. 
• The Company diverted its own rig meant for deep wat er drilling to shallow water 
location and consequently had to forego saving. 
• As a result of failure to make standby well head av ailable by a contractor as per 
contractual provisions, the Company had to pay extra charges. 
• Lack of coordination among various Divisions of the  Company to arrive at a final 
decision for abandonment of continuation of drillin g of a well resulted in extra 
expenditure. 
• As a result of testing two hydrocarbon objects with conventional production testing 
method instead of Modular Dynamic Tester during the course of drilling a well, the 
Company had to incur avoidable expenditure. 
• In deep water drilling operations, several incidents of equipment damage, major and 
minor injuries and in subsequent years many 'near misses' were reported. One fatal 
accident was also reported in February 2006. 
• Time taken for pre-drilling EIAstudies ranged from 21 to 56 months from the date of 
signing respective Production Sharing Contract (PSC ) whereas the exploration 
activities in the NELP blocks were to be undertaken within six months of the award 
of the blocks as per provisions of the production sharing contracts.

for completion of MWP of each phase. Audit observed  that the Company had not

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) to (c) The international oil prices have 
been on consistent up-trend since 2003-04 onwards. Indian basket of crude oil, which 
averaged about $ 23/ bbl at the time of dismantling of Administered Pricing Mechanism 
(APM) in March, 2002 and $ 36/bbl in May 2004, aver aged about $79.25/bbl during 
2007-08. Indian basket of crude oil touched an all time high of $ 112.50/bbI on 28.04.2008.

The main reasons for current high international oil prices are reported as 
follows:—  
(a)  Growth in world oil demand 
(b)  Decline in spare production capacities 
(c)  Worldwide refining bottlenecks 
(d)  Geo-political tensions 
(e)  Decline in Value of dollar 
(f)  Speculation in the international oil market 
(d) While passing on the entire impact of the steep  increase in the international oil 
prices to the consumers would have resulted in a st eep increase in the domestic retail 
prices, the Government is following the principle o f 'Equitable Burden Sharing' under 
which the burden is shared by all the stakeholders, namely:  
Government  Issue of Oil Bonds;  
Oil companies  Upstream/Refinery Discounts;  
Consumers  Minimal Price Increase.  
Despite the steep increase in the international oil prices, the prices of domestic LPG 
and PDS Kerosene have not been increased since Nove mber, 2004 and March, 2002 
respectively. The Government has however made a mar ginal increase in petrol and 
diesel prices by Rs. 2/litre and Re. 1/litre respectively with effect from 15.2.2008.

(a)  whether the second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) has urged framing a 
radical National Law to centralise control over riv er and groundwater in prder to address 
emerging conflicts; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Inter-State water disputes amongst States are increasing and the Central 
Government efforts to resolve the disputes are not fruitful; and 
(d)  if so, the reaction of the Central Government on the views of the Second ARC? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES (SHRI 
JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) In chapter 5  of its Seventh Report, 
containing water related issues, the Second Administrative Reforms Commission does not 
mention any specific suggestion about "framing of radical national law to centralize control 
over river and groundwater in order to address the emerging conflicts".  
The mechanism for settlement of water dispute is already available in the form of Inter 
State River Water Disputes (ISRWD) Act, 1956. The ISRWD Act, 1956 has been amended 
in the year 2002 whereby the adjudication of the water dispute by the tribunal has been made 
time-bound. As per the ISRWD Act, 1956, the water dispute arises among two or more State 
Governments when the Central Government receives re quest under Section 3 of the Act 
from any of the basin States with regard to existence of water dispute. In accordance with the 
said Act, the Central Government is required tc cfer a dispute to a Tribunal after it is satisfied 
that the dispute cannot be settled by negotiations. 
At present there are five water disputes which have  been referred under ISRWD Act, 
1956 namely, Ravi & Beas, Cauvery, Krishna, Mahadayi and Vansadhara river water dispute.  
The water disputes related to Cauvery and Krishna w ere referred to the Tribunals for 
adjudication in 1990 and 2004 respectively. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) 
submitted report and decision under section 5(2) of  the ISRWD Act. 1956 on 5.2.2007. 
Party States and Central Government have sought gui dance/clarification from the tribunal 
under section 5(3) of the Act. Further, party State  have also filed Special Leave Petition 
(SLP) in Hon'ble Supreme Court against the report and decision of the tribunal as mentioned 
above. The Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal passed orders on Interim Relief Applications 
of the States on 9.6.2006.  
The water dispute related to Ravi & Beas was referred to the Ravi & Beas Waters Tribunal 
(RBWT) in 1986 under Section 14 of the said Act. RBWT submitted its report on 30.1.1987 
under section 5(2) of the Act. Party States and Central Government have sought explanation/ 
guidance under section 5(3) of the Act from the Tribunal. The Tribunai has not submitted its 
further report to the Government.  
In respect of Mahadayi River Water Dispute raised by Government of Goa, the Ministry 
of Water Resources is of the opinion that water dispute contained in the request of Government 
of Goa cannot be settled by negotiation. Meanwhile, the Government of Goa filed a suit in 
the Supreme Court for setting up of Water Dispute Tribunal for adjudication, of Mahadayi 
River Water Dispute and an Interlocutory Application (IA) for stay in construction activity 
in September 2006.  
In respect of Vansadhara Water Dispute, the Central Government has not concluded so 
far that the dispute cannot be settled by negotiations. Meanwhile, the Government of Orissa 
has filed a Writ Petition in September, 2006 in the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) Water being a State subject, works for anti-
erosion measures are taken up by the respective State Governments from their own resources 
and according to their own priorities. However, realizing the severity of sea-erosion problems 
in certain critical reaches of the coastal line and on the recommendation of National Coastal

Development Bank (ADB). The Review Mission (1—12th December, 2006) of the ADB in 
their Aide Memoire recommended to work with Karnataka, Goa and Maharashtra.

*541. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI:  
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI:  
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether according to the plan approved by the Union Cabinet, the Planning Commission 
is setting up Inter-Ministerial Working Group to wo rk out the finer details of the reform 
agenda in higher education;

(e)  by when a final decision in this regard is likely to be taken? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (e) In the Eleventh Plan document, the Planning Commission has, inter-alia, suggested 
that an Inter-Ministerial Group should be set up to  work out a detailed reforms agenda in 
higher education. While no such Group has been cons tituted, the University Grants 
Commission (UGC) has initiated steps for academic reforms in higher education by addressing 
all the universities to urgently take up various re forms including the examination reforms 
doing away with annual examination by introducing semester system with continuous internal 
assessment, introduction of credit-based courses, r egular curricula revision, credit 
accumulation and credit transfer system to permit mobility of students. As of now, grant of 
central assistance is not linked to reforms.

According to the provisions of existing Tariff Poli cy of power sector, notified on 6th 
January, 2006, return on investment should attract investments at par with, if not in preference 
to, other sectors so that the electricity sector is able to create adequate capacity. The rate of 
return should be such that it allows generation of reasonable surplus for growth of the sector.  
The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission is to notify, from time to time, the rate of 
return on equity for generation and transmission projects, keeping in view the assessment of 
overall risks and the prevalent cost of capital which shall be followed by the State Electricity 
Regulatory Commissions also. Actual returns vary depedning upon performance on various 
parameters as compared to tariff norms and incentives, if any, for generation beyond threshold 
limits.  
Presently, private investment in the power generati on sector is permitted under the 
competitive tariff bidding route also without any a ssured rate of return. The returns of the 
private developers are dependent upon various factors such as project cost, operating cost, 
operating efficiencies, debt-equity ratio, cost of capital etc. In the case of FDI, besides the 
above, factors such as country risk, foreign exchange risk, availability of alternative investment 
opportunities at home and abroad etc. also influence the expected returns on such investments.  
Accordingly, dividend/return on the FDI investments in the power generation sector would 
vary from case to case based on the above factors.

THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (c) There have been a few reports that the examination centres for the students appearing 
in AIEEE 2008 have not been allotted as per their choices by the CBSE. Specific complaint 
has been received from Maharashtra which has examination centres only in Mumbai, Nagpur 
and Pune, Complaint states that the students have been given centres in Bhopal, Indore etc. 
in place of their choices of Mumbai, Nagpur and Pune.  
Total number of candidates who have appeared a AIEEE 2008 is 862297 as against 641276 
in 2007, which works out to an increase of about 34%. In view of a very large increase in the 
number of candidates, CBSE, which conducts AIEEE, has increased the number of centres 
to 1299 in 2008 as against 1047 in 2007. Out of 862 297 candidates, 806316 candidates, 
(i.e. 93.5%) were allotted examination centres of their choice (1st, 2nd and 3rd choices). As 
there was a tremendous increase in the number of ap pearing candidates, in spite of best 
efforts, CBSE could not accommodate a small percentage (6.5%) of candidates in examination 
centres of their choice.  
However, all girl candidates have been allotted exa mination centres in places of their 
choice.  
More centres will be opened next year and steps wil l be taken to see that to the extent 
possible examination centres are allotted to candidates as per their choice.

Quality of technical education  
*557. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: Will the Minister of H UMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether a meeting of All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) was held in 
the month of December, 2007; 
(b)  whether the meeting was organized to consider ways to enhance access, equity, 
inclusiveness, affordability, relevance and quality of technical education in the country; 
(c)  what were the main decisions arrived at in the meeting; 
(d)  whether Government is making all possible efforts t o take the quality of technical 
education to the next higher level and at par with the highest international standards, and 
(d) whether any concrete steps and measures have been worked out?  
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIARJUN SINGH): 
(a) Yes, Sir. The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) had organized a National 
Conference on Development of Technical Education in India in December, 2007.  
(b)  These issues were discussed in the said conference. 
(c)  The conference had no decision making role. However , some of the important 
suggestions made in the Conference pertained to quality assurance, assessment of manpower 
and skills requirement including expansion of polyt echnics, academic reforms, faculty 
development, industry institute interface and role of AICTE in the changing environment 
and global competitiveness. 
(d)  and (e) The Eleventh Five Year Plan envisages several steps for improvement in the 
quality of technical education including the setting up of new IITs, IIMs, Schools of Planning 
and Architecture, and Indian Institutes of Information Technology etc., revamping of faculty 
development programmes, encouraging research and improvements in curricula, pedagogy, 
accreditation and evaluation system. 
Reservation for disabled in higher education  
*558. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether there is any specific reservation for physically challenged persons in higher 
educational institutions; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the reservation is being complied with; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (d) In terms of the provisions of Section 39  of the Persons with Disabilities (Equal 
Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Partic ipation) Act, 1995 all Government 
eductional institutions and other educational institutions receiving aid from the Government 
shall reserve not less than 3 per cent seats for persons with disabilities. In addition, reservation  

Written Answers to  [6 MAY 2008]  Questions for    143  
Starred & Unstarred  5th May, 2008  
of 3 per cent of teaching and non-teaching post for  employment is also to be made for 
persons with disabilities in these institutions acc ording to the provisions of the said Act. 
Norms are relaxed for persons with disabilities for admission to engineering/technical courses 
and 5 per cent relaxation in marks at the master's level is also given to them for appearing in 
National Eligibility Test (NET) Examination of the University Grants Commission (UGC). 
The Commission also takes into account whether a pa rticular institution is properly 
implementing the provisions of the Act mentioned ab ove, in respect of reservation for the 
persons with disability, while granting development assistance to such an institution.  
Advanced admissions in technical institutions and u niversities  
*559. SHR1 B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of HU MAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether there have been complaints that technical institutions and universities, including 
deemed universities are making admissions well befo re the start of the academic year, 
collecting full fee and retaining the certificates, in a bid to prevent students from moving out 
elsewhere; 
(b)  whether the time-limit for joining courses is being  advanced, thereby restricting the 
options available to students, who tend to take up what comes first; and 
(c)  what steps are being taken to redress those complaints? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Government is aware that i nstitutions and universities including 
deemed to be universities are admitting students to  technical education programmes long 
before the actual starting of an academic session, collecting full fees and retaining the 
certificates in original in order to prevent students from moving out to some other institution. 
This Ministry issued a directive to All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and 
University Grants Commission (UGC) directing them to instruct institutions and universities 
under their control that no institution should keep  in their custody and originals of any 
school or college certificates and that in case a s tudent withdraws before the starting of a 
course, the entire fees collected from the student should be refunded after a deduction of a 
processing fee of not more than Rupees one thousand. It also stated that any violation of the 
above instructions issued by the AICTE/UGC should c all for a punitive action including 
withdrawal of approval and recognition of erring institutions/universities UGC and AICTE 
had accordingly issued necessary instructions to al l the institutions under their control. 
Ministry also had given advice to the Central Educa tional Institutions to follow the above 
stipulation. The AICTE had also issued Public Notices to the above effect in leading national 
dailies and have also placed it on their website (wwe.aicte.ernet.in).

3999. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is proposed to set up mega food parks in North Eastern region, with a view 
to connect the farmers, investors, industries and the markets;  
(b if so, the details thereof;

especially in the backward ones of Bihar, Orissa, J harkhand, Chhattisgarh, etc. to improve

(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCE SSING 
INDUSTRIES (SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAY): (a) to (d) Min istry of Food Processing 
Industries (MFPI) has developed a scheme for providing financial assistance for establishment 
of mega food parks, which envisages a well-defined agri/horticultural-processing zone 
containing State of the art processing facilities with support infrastructure and well established 
supply chain. The scheme aims to provide a mechanism to bring together farmers, processors 
and retailers and link agricultural production to the market so as to ensure maximization of 
value addition, minimization of wastages and improv ing farmers' income. The primaiy 
objective of the scheme is to facilitate establishm ent of an integrated value chain, with 
processing at the core and supported by requisite b ackward and forward linkages. The 
ownership and management of the Mega Food Park woul d vest with a Special Purpose 
Vehicle (SVP) in which organized retailers, processors, service providers, farmers etc. may 
be the equity holders or there may be an anchor investor along with its ancillaries, associated 
companies and others stakeholders. The Government agencies may also be shareholders in 
SPV upto a maximum of 49%.  
The scheme is project oriented. The locations of the Mega Food Parks have to be selected 
on a demand driven, cluster-based approach with delineated supply chain and well supported 
by pre-feasibility studies. Mega Food Parks can be established for any sector on need and 
viability basis such as fruit and vegetables, dairy, meat and poultry etc. or it can also have a 
combination of fruits and vegetables, dairy, meat and poultry etc., the decision on which will 
be taken by the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).  
The scheme intends to incentivise the private sector investment in creating food processing 
infrastructure in a big way. Accordingly, the Scheme envisages financial assistance in the

The scheme provides for establishment of 30 Mega Food Parks with MFPI financial assistance 
of Rs. 1500 crore during the Eleventh Five Year Plan.

4002. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the Minister of FOO D PROCESSING 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that foodgrains worth Rs. 16,500 crores roughly 10 per cent of the 
foodgrains produced, is lost due to bad harvesting timing; 
(b)  whether it is also a fact that 30 per cent of all fruits and vegetables produced, roughly 
worth Rs. 13,600 crores and Rs. 14,000 crores, respectively go waste due to mismanagement 
and lack of storage facilities;

150    Written Answers to  [RAJYASABHA]  Questions for  
Starred & Unstarred  5th May, 2008  
(d) what are the losses in this regard during the period upto February, 2008, as compared to the 
same period of the previous year, year-wise?  
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCE SSING 
INDUSTRIES (SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAY): (a) to (d) According to the report of M/s 
Rabo India Finance Pvt. Ltd., wastage of fruits and vegetables is estimated to be about Rs. 33,000 
crores occurring at various stages of handling afte r harvesting due to fragmented farming, 
provisions in Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development and Regulation) Act, lack of adequate 
post-harvest infrastructure, cold chain facilities, transportation, proper storage facilities etc.  
For promotion of food processing industries which include fruits and vegetables and grain 
processing, financial assistance is provided by Ministry of Food Processing Industries in the form 
of grant under the Scheme of Technology Upgradation/Modernization/ Establishment of food 
processing industries. Under this Scheme, the Ministry extends financial assistance to food 
processing units in the form of grant-in-aid @ 25% of the cost of Plant and Machinery and 
Technical civil works subject to a maximum of Rs. 50.00 lakhs in general areas or 33.33% subject 
to a maximum of Rs. 75.00 lakhs in difficult areas. In order to ensure speedy disbursement of 
the financial assistance, the Ministry has decentralized the disbursement procedure through banks 
under the Scheme of Technology Upgradation/ Modernization/Establishment of food processing 
industries w.e.f. 01.04.07.  
Since one of the major constraints for low level of processing in agro-food products is lack 
of infrastructure such as cold chain facilities and inefficient supply chain, the Ministry has 
developed comprehensive Cold Chain Infrastructure Scheme, during the Eleventh Plan, for creating 
integrated cold chain infrastructure at different levels (i) farm level primary processing centre-
cum-cold chain, (ii) collection/aggregation centres and (iii) Strategic Distribution Centres. The 
initiative being undertaken by the Ministry are aimed at filling the gaps in the supply chain, 
strengthening of cold chain infrastructure leading to overall development of food processing 
industries and reduction in wastages.  
Ministry has also identified thrust areas for strategic intervention for the Eleventh Plan, by 
establishing Mega Food Parks, Cold-chain/value addition and preservation infrastructure, capacity 
building and Human Resource Development by setting up of National Institute of Food 
Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM ), encouraging Research and 
Development, establishment/upgradation of Quality Control Laboratories and various promotional 
activities which would result in increasing the level of processing, value addition of food products, 
including perishables like fruits and vegetables.

(b) and (c) National Curriculum Framework (NCF), 20 05 recommends measures like

rather than rote memory, making examination more fl exible, provision of guidance and 
counselling in schools, and over all to make learning child-centric.  
Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has already taken the following steps to 
reduce stress on students due to examination:—

i. Allowing students to appear in compartmental exa mination immediately after the 
declaration of the result of the main examination. Five chances are given in two 
subjects in class X and one subject in class XII.

counselling facilities centrally to students and parents through telephone and e-mail before 
Xth and Xllth class examinations.

Education cess collected from Assam  
4029. KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  the amount of revenue collected by Government through education cess from Assam; 
(b)  on which educational programme such amount of educa tion cess was spent in that 
State during the last four years; and 
(c)  the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESO URCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (c) As per information received 
from Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue, the State-wise figures regarding collection 
of Education Cess are not maintained. Education Cess is not a part of the net proceeds of the 
divisible pool of sharable taxes based on constitut ional provisions and as per the 
recommendations of the Twelfth Finance Commission. Accordingly, no specific allocation 
is made separately to States/UTs against the amount collected through Education Cess. The 
proceeds of Education Cess credited into Prarambhik  Shiksha Kosh (PSK) are utilized 
exclusively for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and Mid -Day Meal (MDM) Scheme. 
Expenditure on SSA and MDM Scheme is incurred from PSK after the funds provided by 
way of Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) are fully utilized. Assistance under PSK is released 
to States/UTs as per the schematic pattern and budg etary allocation for SSA and MDM 
Scheme.

Private sector participation in higher education  
4033. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Minister has finally agreed to a public-private partnership and increased 
private sector participation in higher education; 
(b)  if so, whether UGC, has developed an action plan/strategy, which acknowledges the 
need for a policy for involving private sector in financing higher education, and has also 
stressed the need to ensure quality; and 
(c)  if so, the concrete measures and steps the Ministry is considering to take for greater 
private sector participation in higher education? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESO URCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) There is currently no bar to 
private participation in the Education sector. The National Policy on Education, 1986 (as 
modified in 1992) encourages non-governmental and voluntary effort in Education, while 
preventing the establishment of institutions which intend to commercialize Education. The 
Policy envisages that "in the interest of maintaining standards and for several other valid 
reasons, the commercialization of technical and professional education will be curbed. An 
alternative system will be devised to involve private and voluntary effort in this sector of 
Education, in conformity with accepted norms and goals". There is already not for profit 
private investment in all sectors of education and the share of such private investment is 
progressively growing, starting from Primary to Higher and Technical Education.  
(b) and (c) According to the information furnished by the University Grants Commission 
(UGC), UGC has constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of Prof. K.B. Power, 
former Secretary General of Association of Indian Universities, to formulate an Action Plan 
for identifying various modes of public-private participation to promote Higher Education.

out rate and emphasized the need to implement the right to education; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof;

(d)  whether Government has sought the help of State Governments and the private sector

DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) to(e) The drop-out rates for 
primary education has reduced by 13.53 percentage p oints between 2001-06 whereas it 
reduced~by only 2.3 percentage point between 1990-2000. At elementary level it has reduced 
by 5.89 percentage point over the same period.

Educational Statistics 2005-06 shows that elementar y level enrolment increased to 18.44 
crore from a level of 17.70 crores in 2003-04.  
The main programmes being implemented by Government of India in partnership with 
the States to reduce drop-outs and achieve universalisation of elementary education, are the 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Mid-Day Meal Scheme.

(b)  whether it is also a fact that since independence, all the British framed laws/rules, etc. 
are enforced even today, and there has been no amendment/replacement thereof; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that due to such laws and rules, etc., the common man is being 
harassed by Government officials; and 
(d) if so, whether there is a proposal under active  consideration to set up an Expert

THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ): (a) No, Sir.  
(b)  Review of all laws, including those enacted during the British era, with a view to 
bring them in harmony with the current economic and social development in the country is 
a continuous process. This task is undertaken by various Ministries/Departments of the Central 
Government administering the respective laws. The Law Commission of India also undertakes, 
from time to time, the study of such laws which may help in achieving the above objectives. 
(c)  and (d) In 1998, the Government set up a Committee on Review of Administrative 
Laws (known as the RC. Jain Commission) with the ob jective of examining the need of 
amendments in the repeal of old/obsolete laws, amon g others. The salient features of the 
recommendations of the said Committee included, among others, amendment of laws/rules, 
review of Acts of critical importance and repeal of  dysfunctional/irrelevant laws. The 
implementation of the report submitted by the said Committee has been undertaken by the 
respective Ministries/Departments and is being moni tored by the Department of 
Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances of the Central Government. The Government 
has also taken steps to bring justice at the doorst eps of the rural masses by setting up of 
Gram Nyayalayas. 
Strength of judges and infrastructure facilities in courts  
4061. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE 
be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Chief Justice of India has recently urg ed Government to increase the 
strength of judges in the country, to cope with the needs and demands; 
(b)  if so, the reaction of Government in this regard; 
(c)  whether several High Courts in the country are not equipped with proper infrastructure 
facilities, resulting into backlog of cases; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government to increas e the strength of judges in various 
courts and to ensure availability of proper infrastructure facilities?  
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ ): (a) to (d) The 
Chief Justice of India, while speaking at the official functions organized by different bodies, 
has urged the Government to increase the strength of Judges in the country to cope with the 
needs of the judiciary.  
The Judge strength of the High Courts was reviewed during 2006 and 2007 and with the 
consent of Chief Justice of India, a total of 152 a dditional posts of Judges in various High 
Courts have been approved. Government has also intr oduced the Supreme Court (Number 
of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2008 in the Lok Sabha on 29.4.2008 for augmenting the judge 
strength of the Supreme Court from the present 25 Judges to 30 Judges excluding the Chief 
Justice of India.

Under Article 235 of the Constitution of India, the administrative control over the Members 
of the subordinate judiciary in the States vests with the concerned High Court and the State 
Government. As such, creation of posts in subordina te judiciary is the concern ofthe State 
Government.  
Providing infrastructural facilities to the High Courts is the responsibility of the concerned 
State Governments. However, to augment the resources ofthe State Governments, the Central 
Government is implementing a scheme for the develop ment of infrastructure facilities for 
the judiciary which includes construction of court buildings and residential accommodation 
for judicial officers/judges. A scheme for comprehe nsive computerization of the District 
and Subordinate Courts based on the National Policy  and Action Plan prepared by the E-
Committee is also currently under implementation.  
Fast track disposal of criminal cases  
4062. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE 
be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Supreme Court has asked the Ministry to  find out whether trial in all 
criminal cases, pending for more than five years, could be fast tracked; 
(b)  whether the Court has also pointed out that if this  proposal is accepted, it could 
potentially revolutionize the criminal justice system; 
(c)  whether the judicial system is presently clogged by  rapid increase in the number of 
criminal cases, without any corresponding increase in the number of trial courts, to handle 
the deluge; and 
(d)  whether the Ministry has considered the proposal and a final decision has been taken? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ): (a) and (b) The 
Supreme Court of India in Transfer Case (Civil) No. 22/2001, Brij Mohan Lai vs. Union of 
India & Others, that inter-alia, deals with matters relating to Fast Track Courts which have 
been constituted for disposal of long pending sessions cases, has in its Order dated 20.11.2007 
mentioned as follows:  
"Having heard Mr. Narasimha, learned amicus curiae and the learned Solicitor General 
of India, we are ofthe opinion that the charts, supplied by the former, may be considered the 
basis by the Law Ministry for arriving at a decisio n in regard to the transfer of cases from 
criminal to civil, and in particular, the cases which are more than 5 years old, for disposal by 
the Fast Track Courts ..." 
(c)  There is an increase in the number of criminal case s in the court, Government has 
taken various measures for facilitating expeditious disposal of criminal cases which include 
setting up of Fast Track courts, amendments to Criminal Procedure Code and Computerisation 
of Courts. The Gram Nyayalayas Bill, 2007 was also introduced to enable setting-up of 
more trial courts in the country at the intermediate Panchayat level. 
(d)  Government is examining the matter.

4065. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of LAW AN D JUSTICE be pleased to

(a) whether, as per the existing system and practice, there is any possibility of accountability 
of judges in their style of functioning;

(b)  if not, what can be the due device for such accountability and the policy of Government in 
this regard; 
(c)  what is the existing system to find out and monitor the evil of corruption prevailing in 
judiciary; and 
(d)  whether there has been a survey to ascertain whether corruption in judiciary is on the 
increase or on the decline? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ): (a) to (c) Judiciary in 
India has functioned independently and enjoys public confidence. The complaints regarding 
corruption in higher judiciary are dealt with by their peers. The Supreme Court in their Full Court 
meeting held on May 7,1997, resolved to devise an in-house procedure to take suitable remedial 
action against Judges who, by their act of omission or commission, do not follow the universally 
accepted values of judicial life including those indicated in the "Restatement of Values of Judicial 
Life". Complaints received against the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts are 
dealt with under "In-House" procedure.  
The Government has, however, introduced the Judges (Inquiry) Bill, 2006 in the Lok 
Sabha on 19.12.2006 which seeks to devise a suitabl e legislative framework for 
empowering a judicial forum to deal with the compla ints against Judges of the Supreme 
Court and High Courts.  
As far as the District and Subordinate Courts are concerned, the respective High Courts 
are empowered to take cognizance of complaints agai nst the members of the Subordinate 
judiciary.  
(d) No, Sir.  
Recruitment of judges  
4066. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  whether there would be a change from the existing s ystem of direct recruitment of 
High Court Judges to a better system, based on merit and objectivity, instead of being mostly 
carried away by the political choice of the ruling State Government, as found at present; and 
(b)  whether there would not be a tinge of favouritism or tune of partiality in pronouncing 
verdicts by judges who were so appointed, to the persons or institutions through whom they 
were appointed? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R, BHARDWAJ ): (a) and (b) 
Pursuant to the Supreme Court Judgement of October 6, 1993 read with their Advisor)' 
Opinion of October 28,1998, the process of initiation of proposal for appointment of Judges 
of the Supreme Court lies with the Chief Justice of India and for the High Court, it lies with 
the Chief Justice of that High Court.  
As per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of Judges drawn on the basis of 
the said judgment, Judges are selected keeping in view their educational qualifications, nature 
and extent of practice, length of the practice the field of specialisation and professional 
income for the last three years. Besides this, the competence of the person, his judicial 
potential, temperament and integrity are also kept in mind. All this information, as also other

as Judges of the Supreme Court/High Courts. As pet;  the above judgment of the Supreme

There is no proposal at present before the Government to bring about any change in the

Appointment of  Judges  
4069. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of LAW  AND JUSTICE be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Pesonnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, in it s recent report, has recommended for 
complete review of the procedure for appointment of judges in various courts; 
(b)  if so, the details in this regard and the views of Government on these recommendations; 
and  
(c) whether Government intends to review the procedure and if so, by when?  
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ ): (a) and (b) In 
their report submitted after examining the Judges ( Inquiry) Bill, 2006 introduced in the 
Lok Sabha on 19.12.2006, the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee has 
favoured for the restoration of the pre-1993 position for appointment of Judges in the Supreme 
Court and the High Courts. They have also suggested mat the appointments could be entrusted 
to a wider body with representation both from the judiciary and the executive.

4093. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to

monitoring of power projects in order to minimize slippages in the capacity addition target

RAMESH): (a) to (d) The Ministry of Power has been actively interacting and monitoring, 
through meeting/discussions with the State Governme nts, BHEL as well as State Power 
Utilities for giving an impetus to various measures  inter-alia the capacity addition. The 
capacity addition programme was discussed in the Ch ief Secretaries' Conference held on 
23rd-24th April, 2007 and Chief Ministers' Conferen ce held on 28th May, 2007 wherein,

the 11th Plan was emphasized. In the Chief Ministers' Conference, it was resolved that the 
Centre and State would ensure timely placement of o rders for all the projects intended to 
give benefit during the 11th Plan and ensure regula r monthly project monitoring for their

chaired by the Minister of Power was held on 24th September, 2007 wherein detailed State-

on 19th February, 2008 wherein expeditious completi on of ordering of all the 11th Plan

Secretaries' Conference convened on 22nd April, 200 8.

monitoring mechanism. States of Goa, Puducherry and Bihar have intimated that they do not

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM

Private companies in power distribution sector  
†4096. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:  
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA:  
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that the power distribution in several parts of the country has been 
handed over to the private companies; 
(b)  if so, the names and locations of the companies engaged in power distribution and the 
year since when the same are engaged in the power distribution work; 
(c)  whether any surveys have been conducted from time t o time, to assess the gains the 
consumers are getting from the work being conducted  by the private companies; and 
(d)  if so, the areas of which companies have been surve yed, along with the dates and 
outcome of the survey? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM 
RAMESH): (a) to (d) Electricity is a concurrent sub ject. Distribution of electricity comes 
within the purview of the States. Accordingly, the Distribution Companies (DISCOMs) are 
regulated by the respective State Electricity Regul atory Commissions (SERCs) under the 
provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003.  
According to the information furnished by Central Electricity Authority (CEA), the details 
of private distribution companies operating in various parts of the country are given in the 
Statement (See below).  
The electricity Act, 2003 provides for specification of performance standards of a licensee 
or a class of licensees by the Appropriate Commissions. Further, the National electricity  
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.  

Written Answers to  [6 MAY 2008]  Questions for   217  
Starred & Unstarred  5th May 2008  
Policy stipulates that appropriate Commission shoul d regulate utilities based on pre-
determined indices on quality of power. Further mor e the Electricity Rules, 2005 notified 
under the Electricity Act, 2003, provide for establishment of Grievance Redressal Forum by 
the distribution licensee for redressal of grievances of consumers. The said Rules also provide 
for appointment of Ombudsman by the State Commissio n under section 42 (6) of the Act 
and he shall inter alia submit his opinion on the licensee's compliance of standards of 
performance as specified by the Appropriate Commission during the preceding six months.  
As the distribution of electricity comes under the purview of the State Governments and 
the State Regulatory commissions, the Central Government does not maintain information 
with regard to compliance of standards of performance by the distribution licensees.  
It has been informed by the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERC) that in a 
survey carried out in early 2007, cross over 10,000  domestic households, majority of the 
consumers preferred the private DISCOMs over the er stwhile Government entity. The 
consumers satisfaction assessed through the survey on a scale of 1 to 10 was in the range of 
5.10 to 5.67 for the three utilities in Delhi. The survey brought out load shedding as major 
consumer concerns which were followed by metering and billing related problems.  
The DERC has further informed that the benefits accruing to the consumers on account 
of the reform process which includes privatization of power in Delhi are as follows:  
(i) The load shedding has reduced by more than 35% from 2001-02 to the present level.  
(ii) The distribution transformer failure rate has reduced from 15% in 2002 to under 2% 
present.  
(iii) With the reduction in AT&C losses from over 5 0% to less than 30%, the revenue 
realization in the distribution sector has increased which has correspondingly had an 
enabling effect on tariffs/Government subsidy.  
Orissa Electricity Regulatory Commission (OERC) has  reported that the Commission 
has appointed Development Support Centre (DSC), Bhubaneshwar to conduct an extensive 
survey on consumer satisfaction.

   Supply of equipment for power projects  
4101. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHART1A: 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:  
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the power equipment manufacturing companies  are unable to provide 
equipments for various power projects, resulting in the delay in implementation of power 
schemes; 
(b)  if so, the facts and the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Central Electricity Authority (CE A) has expressed concern over the delay 
in supply of crucial parts and lack of gas supplies for power projects; and 
(d) if so, the reaction of Government thereto and t he strategies to be made to ensure 
availability of inputs for power projects?  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM 
RAMESH): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. There have been delays in implementation of some power 
projects due to non availability of timely supplies from the power equipment manufacturing 
companies. The details of projects that have been delayed during the Tenth Plan due to delay 
in supplies/erection by suppliers/contractors is given in the Statement (See below).  
(c) and (d) The Ministry of Power through Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has been 
regularly monitoring the progress of ongoing projec ts and sensitising all the stakeholders 
about the prevailing bottlenecks including the delay in supply. The steps taken to overcome 
the supply constraints include:—  
• According to information received from Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), 
it has enhanced its capacity to deliver 10,000 MW o f main plant equipment per 
annuam. Furthermore, they have put in place an action plan to enhance capacity to 
deliver 15,000 MW per annum by December, 2009. 
• A Joint Venture Agreement has been signed between NTPC Ltd. and BHEL to take 
up work related to Engineering, Procurement and Con struction (EPC) for power 
plants and other infrastructure projects. NTPC Ltd.  has also entered into an 
Memorandum of Understanding with Bharat Forge Limited to promote a joint venture 
company initially to take up the manufacture of castings, forgings, fittings and high 
pressure pipings. 
• M/s L&T has already formed a Joint Venture Company with MHI, Japan for 
manufacture of supercritical steam generator and steam turbine generators in India. 
Certain other manufacturers viz., M/s Skoka Power, India Ansoldo, Italy Cethar 
Vessels, India have also expressed interst in setti ng up manufacturing facilities for 
boiler and turbine generators in the country. 
• All stakeholders have been sensitized towards enlar ging the vendor base so as to 
meet the Balance of Plant (BoP) requirements. 
While firming up the capacity addition target for E leventh Plan, only the projects 
where gas supply is already tied up have been considered.

Independent regulatory body for power sector  
4105. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to  
state:  
(a)  whether with the private sector participation in the power generation sector, Govern-
ment is proposing to set up an independent regulatory body, to oversee the role and partici-
pation of the players in the energy sector; 
(b)  if so, what would be the broad objectives of the regulator; 
(c)  the place where it would be situated and by when it would commence its operations; 
and 
(d)  if not, the reasons for not setting up of such regu lators, when the players have in-
creased in the recent past? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM 
RAMESH): (a) to (c) An independent regulatory struc ture for the power sector already 
exists. The Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act,  1998 provided for constitution of a 
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) an d for creation of State Electricity 
Regulatory Commissions (SERCs). SERCs were also constituted under the respective State 
Electricity Reforms Acts.  
The Electricity Act, 2003 also provides for constitution of a Central Electricity Regula-
tory Commission (CERC) by the Central Government an d State Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions by the State Governments. After the enactment of the Electricity Act, 2003, 
the CERC and the SERCs already constituted were deemed to have been constituted under 
the provisions of the Elecricity Act, 2003 and continue to functions as such. In so far as the 
State of Jammu & Kashmir is concerned, the regulatory commissions has been constituted 
under its own Act.  

228 Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Questions for  
Starred & Unstarred  5f/i May 2008  
The CERC, which was constituted under the ERC Act, 1998 is located at Delhi and the 
SERCs in their respective States. The Central Government under section 83 of the Electric-
ity Act, 2003 has also constituted a Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) for the 
States of Manipur and Mizoram and the head office of the Commission is located at Aizwal. 
Further, the Central Government has also notified a JERC for the Union Territories except 
Delhi, since the Govt. of NCT of Delhi had already constituted the Delhi Electricity Regula-
tory Commission (DERC).  
The functions of the Electricity Regulatory Commiss ions are wide ranging and include 
functions such as grant of licence for transmission , distribution and trading of electricity, 
tariff regulation"and tariff determination of generating companies, tariff determination for 
intra and inter-State transmission of electricity, tariff determination for retail sale of electric-
ity, specification and enforcement of standards wit h respect to quality, continuity and 
reliability of service by licencees, adjudication of disputes, and promotion of generation of 
electricity from renewable sources of energy.  
The Electricity Act also provides for establishment of an Appellate Tribunal for Electric-
ity to hear appeals against the orders of adjudicat ing officers or the Regulatory Commis-
sions under the Act; this Tribunal also functions as the Appellate Tribunal for the purposes 
of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006 under Section 30 of that Act.  
(d) Does not arise in view of (a) to (c) above.

4107. SHRIB. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is proposed to conserve around 10,000 mw power during the Eleventh Five Year 
Plan through efficient technology; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)  what is the action plan of Government to promote and develop renewable energy in a big 
way to bridge the growing gap between demand and supply? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM 
RAMESH):(a)Yes,Sir.  
(b)  The Ministry of Power has formulated 8 schemes to promote energy efficiency in the 
country which include the Bachat Lamp Yojana, Stand ards and Labelling scheme, Energy 
Conservation Building code, Agricultural and Munici pal Demand Side Management, 
Operationalising Energy Conservation Act, 2001 by Strengthening Institutional Capacity of State 
Designated Agencies, Energy Efficiency in Small and  Medium Engterprises, Institutional 
Strengthening of Bureau of Energy Efficiency and other Energy Efficiency Institutions and 
Contribution to State Energy Conservation Fund. 
(c)  The Electricity Act, 2003 mandates all States to fix a certain minimum percentage for 
purchase of Power from renewable energy sources in the area of distribution licensee depending 
on resource availability and local conditions. Furt her, the Government has taken several 
measures to popularize the use of renewable energy systems/devices in the country which 
include the following: 
 
• Fiscal and financial incentives, such as, capital/interest subsidy, accelerated 
depreciation, nil/concessional excise and customs duties; 
• Preferential tariff for grid interactive renewable power in most potential States; 
• Extensive publicity and awareness on the use of renewable energy systems/devices 
through print, postal and electronic media;

• Organization of special events like the Rajiv Gandhi Akshay Urja Diwas; 
• Constitution of District-level Advisory Committees in the States to facilitate effective 
coordination of renewable energy schemes/programmes. 
During the Eleventh Plan period it is proposed to add power generation capacity of 15,000 
MW from renewable sources and deploy 11.6 million s q. meter of solar thermal collector 
area for water heating, cooking, drying application s and 2 million cubic meter aggregate 
capacity of family type biogas plants. Provision of renewable energy systems for electricity/

Merchant Power Plants 
4108. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:  
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether in its effort to achieve a power capacity addition of 78,577 MW, the Ministry 
had envisaged capacity addition of around 15,000 MW, by tapping Merchant Power Plants; 
(b)  whether Government's plans have come a cropper as it now looks at an entirely new 
policy for Merchant Power Plants (MPPs), with its earlier policy failing to attract bidders; 
(c)  what are the 24 sites which have been considered for MPPs in the country; and 
(d)  what are the concrete measures taken to enhance capacity of 15,000 MW from MPPs? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM 
RAMESH): (a) to (d) According to the Report of the Working Group on Power for Eleventh 
Plan, a capacity addition of about 10,000-12,000 M W is envisaged during the Eleventh Plan 
period through Merchant Power Plants (MPPs). This capacity has not been taken into acount 
while working out the required capacity during the Eleventh Plan.  
Unlike conventional power plants with tied-up Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), MMPs 
compete for customers and absorbe the full market risk. Typically the risk of MPP is carried 
on the balance sheet of the promoter. Cosequent to enactment of the Electricity Act, 2003, 
thermal generation has been de-licensed and the developer has to tie-up site and other inputs 
required to set up power plants.  
Government has taken several measures for facilitat ing the development of MPPs 
such as:  
• The National Electricity Policy, 2006, provides that a part of new generating capacity 
of about 15% may be sold outside long term PPAs. 
• Under the new Hydro Policy, 2008, private developers have been given the facility 
of 40% merchant sale in the power generation [after deducting free power to the host 
State(s)]. 
• Open access in transmission has been introduced in the Electricity Act, 2003 which 
would enable the MPPs to have connectivity with the National Grid through Regional 
Grid/State Grid. In distribution open access is to be introduced in phases. For 
consumers with requirement of more than one Mega Wa tt, open access is to be 
mandatorily introduced by January, 2009.

Inaccurate power meters  
4112. SHRI N. R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the domestic electricity meters, installed by distribution companies in the capital, 
run about 2.5 per cent fast, resulting in inflated power bills; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Electricity Consumers Advocate Committee (ECAC) has approached the 
Central Electricity Authority, for reducing and reviewing the accuracy of electricity meters from 
2.5 per cent to 0.5 per cent; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHR I JAIRAM  
RAMESH): (a) and (b) Electricity is a concurrentsubject. Distribution of electricity comes  
within the purview of the States. Accordingly, thte distribution companies (DISCOMs) are  
regulated by the respective State Electricity. Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) under the  
"provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003.  
The Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission has reported that the accuracy standards of 
different classes of electricity meters are decided by Bureau of India Standards (BIS). The 
current standard for domestic electricity meters issued by BIS provide for a tolerance of + 2.5 per 
cent. Therefore, a meter found to be fast or slow within the prescribed limit of + 2.5 percent 
is considered to be functioning accurately and, therefore, does not have any billing related 
implications.

Fast-running electricity meters  
4113. SHRIN. R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the electricity meters installed by the private power companies, particularly 
in Delhi, run very fast and register excess units of electicity, than actually utilized; 
(b)  if so, whether Government has received any complaints regarding this; 
(c)  if so, whether Government has conducted any inquiry in this regard; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, along with the action t aken by Government against such 
complaints; and 
(e) whether Government proposes to check the monopo ly of private power distribu 
tion companies and their arbitrary behaviour, in Delhi?  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE, MINISTRY 
OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY AND MINISTER OF STATE IN T HE MINISTRY 
OF POWER (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH) : (a) to (e) Electric ity is a concurrent subject. 
Distribution of electricity comes within the purview of the States. Accordingly, the Distribu-
tion Companies (DISCOMs) are regulated by the respe ctive State Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions (SERCs) under the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003.  
In terms of Section 146 of the Electricity Act, 2003, any person including the DISCOMs 
is liable to be prosecuted for non-compliance with any order or direction given under the Act 
or for contravention or attempting or abetting the contravention of any other provisions of 
the Act or of any Rules or Regulations made thereunder.  
Section 14 of the Electricity Act provides that the appropriate Electricity Regulatory. 
Commission may grant a licence to two or more persons for distribution of electricity through 
their own distribution system within the same area, subject to specified conditions.  
Section 55 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides that no licensee shall supply electricity 
after the expiry of two years from the appointed date except through installation of a correct 
meter in accordance with the regulations to be made in this behalf by the Central Electricity 
Authority (CEA). CEA has notified the Central Elect ricity Authority (Installation and 
Operation of Meters) Regulations, 2006 on 17.3.2006 .  
The Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission .(DERC) has informed that in recent years 
a number of meter testing drives have been conducted by the DISCOMs, the Government of 
NCT of Delhi and by the DERC, and the number of met ers found to be running fast out of 
those tested was small. The SERC of Kerala has info rmed that no case of energy meter 
running fast has been received.  
According to the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC), the joint inspec-
tion report of Government Electrical Inspector, con sumer representatives and licensee of 
the digital meters installed by the licencee do not reveal that digital meters are unreliable.
