4126. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM: Will the  Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND 
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Special Component Plan (SCP)/Tribal sub-Plan (TSP) for SCs and STs 
incorporated in every Five Year Plan since 1979, has failed to make much headway due to its 
faulty implementation, with the several Government departments totally ignoring it;  
(b) whether, according to a recent study, not only the proportions of these Plan 
allocations are far below the proportion of SC/ST population in the total population of the 
country, but also many of the mainstream Ministries have not been showing any allocations 
clearly earmarked for SCs;  
(c)  whether Government has considered the report fully; and 
(d)  what concrete meassures are proposed during the current Plan?

EMPOWERMENT (SHRIMATI SUBBULAKSHMI JAGADEESAN): (a)  to (d) As per 
available information, many of the Ministries/Depar tments are not separately earmarking 
funds under Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP) (earlier known as Special Component Plan) 
and Tribal Sub Plan (TSP). The Planning Commission,  in December, 2006 has issued 
consolidated guidelines on formulation, implementation and monitoring of SCSP and TSP 
to Central Ministries/Department. These guidelines, inter alia, include earmarking of funds

proportion of SC and ST population to the total population and placing the earmarked funds

to review the implementation of the Special strategies of Special Component Plan (SCP) for 
Scheduled Castes and the Tribal Sub Plan for Schedu led Tribes and to resolve various 
policy-related issues thereto in respect of central Ministries/Departments as well as the State/

4133. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of TRIBAL  AFFAIRS be pleased to

standards of people residing in plains? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFF AIRS (DR. 
RAMESHWAR ORAON): (a) and (b) In addition to the se veral Central Sector/Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes/ programmes being implemented by Ministry of Tribal Affairs for the 
welfare and development of tribal people in the cou ntry, this Ministry has launched a new 
initiative in the year 2005-06 for the development of foest villages. It has also enacted the 
Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwell ers (Recognition of Forest Rights) 
Act, 2006.  
Under the scheme of Development of Forest Villages, funds are released to the States for 
integrated development of forest villages by provid ing basic minimum services and 
facilities like approach roads, health care, primar y education, minor irrigation, rain water 
harvesting, drinking water, sanitation, community halls etc.  
The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) 
Act, 2006, which has been operationised with effect  from 31.12.2007, seeks to recognize 
and vest certain rights over forest land in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Tradi-
tional Forest Dwellers who have been residing in su ch forests for generations but where 
rights could not be recorded to ensure (a) tenurial security, providing them relief against the 
physical and psychological alienation from land belonging to them; (b) livelihood, in terms 
of agriculture and ownership of minor forest produc e, including right to collect, use, and 
dispose the same; and (c) traditional and customary rights.  
(c) The main thrust of present schemes/programmes of tribal development is to bring the 
tribals into the mainstream and upto the national levels.

†4138. SHRI MOTILALVORA:

children;

(d)  if not, the reasons therefor?

DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b ) Yes, Sir. The 
Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing following Schemes for destitute 
and neglected children:—

(ii) An Integrated Programme for Street Children; and  
(iii) Scheme for Assistance to Homes (Shishu Greh) to Promote In-country Adoption.

4139. SHRI B.J. PANDA:  
MS. MABEL REBELLO:  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that there is still no end to women trafficking in the North Eastern 
Region; 
(b)  if so, what is the extent of this menace; and 
(c)  what is the short-term and long-term action plan of Government to combat this menace? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) to (c)  There are reports 
about incidents of trafficking of women in the North Eastern Region. The Immoral Traffic 
(Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA) supplemented by the Indian Penal Code prohibits trafficking

for traffickers. The ITPA is now being further amen ded providing for more stringent 
punishment for trafficking in persons including children. The Ministry of Women and Child 
Development conducts advocacy, awareness generation and sensitization programmes for 
prevention of child trafficking. The Central Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Women 
and Child Development on combating Child Prostitution quarterly reviews the State's activities 
in combating trafficking and prostitutions. The Ministry of Women and Child Development

4144. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the Minister of WOMEN  AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the dowry prohibition law is in force in the country; 
(b)  if so, the number of cases booked for violation during the last ten years; 
(c)  whether it is a fact that the law is not being implemented; 
(d)  if so, the reasons therefor; and

DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) Yes, Sir.

Governments within their mechanisms. The Central Government has further advised all 
State Governments to appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers with independent charge and to 
notify rules under the Act.

has taken a number of steps to raise the status of women and to change the societal attitudes 
towards girls and women. These include media campaigns, awareness generation camps, 
spreading legal literacy, counselling, legal aid, support to voluntary agencies and schemes 
for socio-economic empowerment of women. These initiatives of the Government are a 
continuous process.

Children on the footpaths  
4147. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government is aware ofthe report of United Nations about the children 
living on the footpaths in a large number of big me tro cities and also in small towns ofthe 
country; 
(b)  if so, the reaction of Government thereon; 
(c)  whether the number of orphans in the country has in creased during the last three 
years; 
(d)  whether Government proposes to simplify the adoption law, to facilitate adoption of 
orphans; and 
(e)  if so, by when Government is likely to reframe such laws? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) Government is not 
aware of any recent report of United Nations about children living on footpaths in India. The 
Census data also does not have information on street children. However, it is known that a 
large number of children are living on streets in the country, UNICEF estimated 11 million 
street children in 1994.  
(c)  There is no Government data on number of orphans in the country. 
(d)  and (e) The legal adoption procedure of orphaned, abandoned and surrendered children 
is very organized and structured and only agencies recognized by the State Governments 
can place children in adoption both in-country and inter-country. Central Adoption Resource 
Agency (CARA) is the only nodal agency at national level for adoption matters and issues 
guidelines for adoption from time to time. The proc edures governing in-country adoption 
and inter-country adoption have been provided under "Guidelines for In-country Adoption 
2004 and Guidelines Adoption from India 2006", respectively. These guidelines are subject 
to regular review in order to make them more effici ent and child friendly. The Juvenile 
Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment  Act, 2006 along with Model Rules 
2007 under this Act, also aims to provide a child friendly and simple adoption framework.

single scheme known as 'Support to NGOs/Institutions/SRCs for Adult Education and Skill 
development". The proposed changes in schemes are without affecting any change in the NLM.

authority. 
(c)  Does not arise.
